analysis.title: LandBridge (LB): First Take: 3Q26 In-Line and 2026 Guidance Raised After M&A; First Major Data Center Lease Signed
key_insights: LandBridge (LB, Buy) reported 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of $64m, in line with GSe of $64m and above FactSet consensus of $60m. Higher surface use revenue offset modestly lower produced water growth versus the GS model.
3Q26 FCF was $49m versus GSe of $44m and FactSet consensus of $48m.
LB raised its FY26 EBITDA guide to $220-235m from $210-230m, versus GSe of $244m and consensus of $228m. GS sees the guide as potentially conservative as commercial activity ramps.
The guide implies 4Q26 EBITDA of $52-67m, down 7% QoQ and 22% below GSe, likely because of the size of M&A contributions.

LB has acquired about 34k acres through 3Q26 for about $275m, including about 25,000 acres in the Delaware Basin. The initial purchase multiple is about 10x, representing about $27m of EBITDA contribution. GS 2026 estimates already include about $8m.

Management sees the multiple falling to sub-6x near term, with line of sight to about 6x from pore space monetization alone. Reaching the $3,000/acre Surface Use Economic Efficiency target implies about 3x, or about $92m run-rate EBITDA.

LB announced its first definitive data center lease. Affiliate PowerBridge exercised its option to lease 825 acres for Alpha Phase I of the Alpha Digital campus, which is more than 300 MW of a planned 2 GW and scalable to about 3,400 acres.

The agreement includes a long-term ground lease and a power royalty tied to electricity generation. Terms were not disclosed. Construction began in September 2026, with initial power delivery projected for 4Q27.

GS notes LB has previously pointed to $10-40m per GW, which would put 300 MW at roughly $3-12m of revenue on the first phase. The PowerBridge customer is not disclosed and GS expects a near-term announcement.

GS calls the release constructive following weak share price performance on the day. It believes behind-the-meter power solutions in the Permian are positioned to take a broader share of the data center market.
Produced water royalty volumes were 2,153 kb/d, 2% below GSe of 2,188 kb/d and up 8% QoQ. The quarter had a full contribution from Speedway I and Kraken MVC increases.
Surface Use royalties and revenues of $54m beat GSe of $52m on better easement and surface revenue. Resource Sales and Royalties of $13m and Oil and Gas Royalty revenue of $4m were in line with GSe.

market_movers.rationale: Buy and $97 12-month target on 24.0x 2027E EBITDA, 40.1% upside from $69.26. GS sees the quarter and the PowerBridge lease as constructive.

Execution on additional commercial opportunities including data centers.
Clarity around the capital returns profile.
